title: When will the blue stars meet next?
description: Two rows of stars repeat their colours every six and every four stars. Both rows are blue at the fourth star, and the lowest common multiple of six and four shows when the blue stars meet again. The answer is checked by listing the blue stars of both rows.
teaching_notes: One idea: two patterns that repeat meet again after the lowest common multiple of their lengths. Ask the class to list the blue stars of both rows before the working is shown. Watch for students who count from the first star and not from the fourth.

source: End of chapter Figure it Out, Q1
video_script.why: The child has used the lowest common multiple to find when two events happen together and now uses it for two repeating rows of coloured stars.
video_script.substitution: Find where each row is blue, then add the lowest common multiple of the two row lengths to the first shared blue star.
video_script.anchor: Two rows of coloured stars, one under the other, the first repeating six colours and the second repeating four colours.
video_script.payoff_line: The blue stars meet next at the sixteenth star
never_show: 12 as the star where the blue stars meet
maths_rules: row one repeats yellow, green, orange, blue, pink, grey: 6 stars, blue at the 4th, 10th, 16th
row two repeats green, orange, yellow, blue: 4 stars, blue at the 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th
both rows are blue at the 4th star
4 + 12 = 16, so the blue stars meet next at the 16th star
video_script.design: One idea: repeating rows meet again after the lowest common multiple of their lengths. The two rows stay on the board and the blue stars are lit one row at a time.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Two rows of stars repeat their colours.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The first row repeats yellow, green, orange, blue, pink and grey.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>The second row repeats green, orange, yellow and blue.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>When will the blue stars meet next?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>A row that repeats starts again after a fixed number of stars.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The first row repeats after six stars. The second row repeats after four stars.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The smallest number that both six and four go into is called their lowest common multiple.

beats.on_screen: Given: row one repeats every 6 stars, blue at the 4th; row two repeats every 4 stars, blue at the 4th

marks.m1: the given line is written in the working band

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, two rows of stars that repeat their colours, with blue in both.

beats.on_screen: To find: the next star where both rows are blue

marks.m1: the find line is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find the next star where both rows are blue. We solve it the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: row one has blue at the 4th star and repeats every 6; row two has blue at the 4th star and repeats every 4; both are blue at the 4th star

marks.m1: the blue star in row one is lit at the fourth place
marks.m2: the blue star in row two is lit at the fourth place
marks.m3: the two lit stars are joined by a line

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, in the first row the blue star is the fourth star.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>In the second row the blue star is also the fourth star.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The two rows are blue together at the fourth star.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 6 = 2 × 3 and 4 = 2 × 2, so the LCM is 2 × 2 × 3 = 12
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, six is two times three, and four is two times two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The lowest common multiple is two times two times three, which is twelve.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: the next shared blue star is 12 stars after the 4th, so 4 + 12 = 16

marks.m1: an arrow of length 12 stars starts at the fourth star
marks.m2: 4 + 12 = 16 is written at the end of the arrow

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, both rows repeat together after every twelve stars.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The next shared blue star is twelve stars after the fourth. Four plus twelve is sixteen.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, check: row one is blue at the 4th, 10th, 16th; row two is blue at the 4th, 8th, 12th, 16th

marks.m1: the blue stars of row one are lit at the fourth, tenth and sixteenth places
marks.m2: the blue stars of row two are lit at the fourth, eighth, twelfth and sixteenth places
marks.m3: the sixteenth place is lit in both rows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check by listing the blue stars. The first row is blue at the fourth, tenth and sixteenth.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The second row is blue at the fourth, eighth, twelfth and sixteenth.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>After the fourth, the first place in both lists is the sixteenth.

marks.m1: the answer At the 16th star is written and boxed

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The blue stars meet next at the sixteenth star.
